title: Handover Pages and Checkpoints
eyebrow: Design for approval, second version · nothing built yet
replyPrefix: Design approved: handover pages and checkpoints

short.lead: This happens in two steps, in this order. First, the page template stops being one fixed shape: it gains places for pictures, and each project sets its own look and how visual its pages are. Then the checkpoints from the first version of this design make the template mandatory. Your plunderspell page shows why the order matters: when it was forced into today's template, the render of the Wick and the Ophan was dropped, and that render was the most useful thing on the page.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: Any In short step, Changes item or choice option can carry a captioned picture that opens full width on tap. A Changed item can show a before-and-after pair: side by side on a wide screen, and a slider to drag between them on a phone.
Each project sets its own look

A file in the project, docs/page-style.json, sets the page's colours, fonts and how visual it must be. Plunderspell would require pictures for art and visual changes, while this repository would leave them optional. A project without the file gets today's look.
Nothing from you now. Later you can adjust a project's file, or ask me to.

A script takes the page's content and the project's style file and writes the page, so no page is copied from the template by hand. It refuses a visual project's page when an art or visual change has no picture.

These are the checkpoints from the first version of this design: fixed points where a missed rule stops the turn. A reply that offers choices, lays out a plan or runs over 200 words can't end without a page. A page the builder didn't make is refused when it is saved or published.
A line in the decisions log, then a build plan with an issue for each step.
You answer the eight choices (the Choices step) and send your reply.

Checkpoint table (in hook.py)
One list: the moment, the rule, and whether it blocks or reminds.

The first three checkpoints fire when a reply ends, when a page is saved, and when it is published. The first two enforce both the page rule and the editor helper (the check that a page has had an editing pass); publishing enforces the page rule only.
A rule's detail is read only if I choose to read it. The rule loaded at session start never names the template.
A table of fixed points, each tied to a rule and to what happens when it is missed.
You can see in one place what is enforced and when, and a missed rule stops the turn instead of passing quietly.

End-of-reply check (the handover part of hook.py)
From a reminder to a single block.
Reminds only. The architecture doc records that it never blocks.
Sends me back once if a reply proposes something with no page, or if a page has had no editing pass. On the retry it only reports, so it can't loop.
This is the same safety the subagent commit check already uses: the retry is marked as a retry, and on it the check reports and lets the turn end.

wrapup.summary: Make the page template flexible first, with pictures and a style for each project, then make it mandatory with checkpoints that block once.
wrapup.changing: The page template, a new style file for each project, a new page builder, the end-of-reply check, a new check before a page is saved or published, the rule loaded at session start, and how rules load after an update.
wrapup.blocking: Your approval of this design and your answers to the eight choices.
